title: UniFi Network Application 11.0.103
summary:
Overview

UniFi Network Application 11.0.103 requires UniFi OS 6.0 or newer and includes the improvements and bugfixes below.

If you are upgrading from 10.x or earlier versions, note that the PostgreSQL migration clears existing statistics history, and all sites are automatically migrated to Zone-Based Firewall. See 11.0.97 for details.

Improvements

  • Added support for matching networks in the External zone as Firewall Policy destinations.

Bugfixes

  • Fixed a rare issue where VPN Servers could fail to work.

  • Fixed a rare issue where UID Enterprise WiFi networks could fail to work.

  • Fixed an issue where Firewall Policies between networks could lose IPv6 port restrictions after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Forwarding rules to networks routed by a Layer 3 switch did not work.

  • Fixed an issue where WAN OUT block rules could stop blocking VPN client traffic after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed a rare issue where the Devices page could fail to load.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Forwarding rules to hosts behind a static route could stop working after upgrading from Network 10.6 with Legacy Firewall enabled.

  • Fixed a rare issue where upgrading to Network 11.0 could fail.

Additional information

 

Self-Hosted UniFi Deployments

For self-hosted deployments, we recommend transitioning to UniFi OS Server, which provides the full UniFi OS Platform experience, including the latest features, improvements, and integrations.

UniFi Cloud Gateways remain our recommended solution for deployments that do not require self-hosting.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Water and Wastewater Systems
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: United States

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-117659
The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.

If you are an offline customer (InfoScan has no internet access), you will need to download the update from the Dorsett Controls Customer Portal by selecting the InfoScan Update tile, downloading the update, and following the instructions listed on the portal.

Mitigation
Maintain strict inbound firewall policies (such as Windows Defender Firewall) blocking external traffic on port 7782. This is already the case by default on standard Windows installations. If remote access is required, restrict traffic via a secure, authenticated channel (e.g., a VPN or SSH tunnel) rather than opening direct inbound firewall rules.

title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
summary:
Purpose

CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938. This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK). Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution.

Actions to take

CISA urges organizations to take the following actions:

  • Identify affected Java installations. Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances. Note: JDKs and Java runtimes may not appear as separate entries in software inventories.
  • Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available, prioritizing internet-facing systems.
    • If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access.
  • Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions.
  •  Monitor for indicators of suspicious activity, including rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes.

title: Formlabs dropped the Raspberry Pi on the way to a $699 SLA printer
summary:
Formlabs sent me a Form Studio 1 resin 3D printer to test after years of back-and-forth about their Form 4 printer.

title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
summary: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

title: Radxa's Q8B has 2x the performance and expansion of the Pi 5
summary:
There was a time I'd look at a board like the Radxa Dragon Q8B (at left, above) and be like, "there's no way I'd spend $209 on an SBC with 8 gigs of RAM". But we're in 2026, and seeing the 8 gig Raspberry Pi 5 going for almost the same amount, I figured I'd give it a shot.

On paper, the Q8B beats the Pi 5 in pretty much every way. A lot of that is thanks to this Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 chip, which is the same chip I tested on Microsoft's Windows Dev Kit 2023.

title: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
summary: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. KrebsOnSecurity has learned that the suspect, who uses the hacker handle "Rey," was detained as ShinyHunters was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by the global aerospace company Boeing, which manufactures the fleet of planes used by the employer of Rey's father -- Royal Jordanian Airlines.

title: I'm starting HomelabFest (in St. Louis, Sep 2027)
summary:
I've been working on my homelab for years, and I enjoy sharing what I learn through this blog and my YouTube channel.

Over the past few years, I realized the homelab community (which isn't really a defined thing—that's okay) hasn't had its own gathering, the way makers, software engineers, embedded developers, and HPC professionals do.

There are many events that have crossover into the homelab realm, but nothing focused on energy-efficient servers, privacy-respecting self-hosted software, keeping old hardware useful, or cable management and rackmounting on a budget.

title: Raspberry Pi locks down Pi 5 RAM upgrades in firmware
summary:
Raspberry Pi added a feature in their firmware that restricts users from swapping RAM chips, sometimes even RAM chips of the same capacity from other Raspberry Pi boards.

Apparently there were people buying cheap 1 or 2 gig Pi 5s, soldering in some cheap and sometimes unreliable 8 gig RAM chips, and selling them as new 8 gig Pi 5s.

Now I totally understand where Raspberry Pi's coming from. They don't wanna support Pis being sold like this, because flaky RAM and dodgy resellers are a huge problem. Especially with how profitable can be in the current AI bubble.

title: NTP, an atomic clock, and having a great time at the world's largest VCF
summary:
I'm back from VCF Midwest 21, arguably the largest vintage computer festival on the planet.

After being blown away last year, I decided to get a table of my own this year, to demonstrate NTP Time on a bunch of old Macs, representing every era up to the pinnacle of the PowerPC, an Xserve G5 (serving duty as a Stratum 2 ntpd server).

Attending as an exhibitor is a lot different. In some ways better (I got to interact face-to-face with at least 200 people—after that I ran out of my 'time tokens'), and in some ways worse (I only got to see about 10% of the exhibits—if that).
